(3) Entropy estimation over continuous, high-dimensional state spaces. Both terms in the empowerment decomposition–the marginal entropy of reachable futures H(St+k∣st)H(S_{t+k} \mid s_t) and the conditional entropy H(St+k∣st,At:t+k)H(S_{t+k} \mid s_t, A_{t:t+k})–require evaluating entropies of distributions over the state space. For realistic sensorimotor systems, this state space is continuous and high-dimensional (joint angles, visual features, spatial coordinates, etc.), making exact entropy computation intractable. In practice, this demands two interacting capabilities: (a) a compressed, low-dimensional state representation that mitigates the curse of dimensionality (connecting empowerment computation directly to the compression/representation-learning objective discussed previously), and (b) an entropy estimation method that operates within that compressed space – e.g., analytic computation under parametric forward models, k-nearest-neighbor estimators, or learned variational bounds. (a) and (b) are not independent engineering choices but co-constrained: the geometry of the learned representation determines which estimation methods are tractable (a Gaussian latent space admits closed-form conditional entropies; a discrete codebook reduces the problem to combinatorial counting), and conversely, the desire for tractable entropy estimation can serve as an inductive bias on the compression scheme itself. For instance, if the forward model in latent space is trained to produce Gaussian predictive distributions, The concepts are summarized schematically (Figure).

P(zt+k∣zt,at:t+k)=𝒩(μθ(zt,at:t+k),Σθ(zt,at:t+k)),\begin{equation} P(z_{t+k} \mid z_t, a_{t:t+k}) = \mathcal{N}\bigl(\mu_\theta(z_t, a_{t:t+k}),\; \Sigma_\theta(z_t, a_{t:t+k})\bigr), \end{equation}

then the conditional entropy for any specific action sequence has a closed-form solution,

H(Zt+k∣zt,at:t+k)=12log⁡det⁡(2πeΣθ(zt,at:t+k)),\begin{equation} H(Z_{t+k} \mid z_t, a_{t:t+k}) = \frac{1}{2} \log \det \bigl(2\pi e\, \Sigma_\theta(z_t, a_{t:t+k})\bigr), \end{equation}

and the full conditional entropy term can be obtained by averaging over the action distribution: The concepts are summarized schematically (Figure).

H(Zt+k∣zt,At:t+k)=𝔼p(at:t+k)[12logdet(2πeΣθ(zt,at:t+k))].\begin{equation} H(Z_{t+k} \mid z_t, A_{t:t+k}) = \mathbb{E}_{p(a_{t:t+k})} \left[ \frac{1}{2} \log \det \bigl(2\pi e\, \Sigma_\theta(z_t, a_{t:t+k})\bigr) \right]. \end{equation}

The marginal entropy H(Zt+k∣zt)H(Z_{t+k} \mid z_t) is more demanding: it requires marginalizing over the (optimized) action distribution to obtain the mixture

P(zt+k∣zt)=∫p*(at:t+k)P(zt+k∣zt,at:t+k)dat:t+k,\begin{equation} P(z_{t+k} \mid z_t) = \int p^*(a_{t:t+k})\, P(z_{t+k} \mid z_t, a_{t:t+k})\, da_{t:t+k}, \end{equation}

which is a mixture of Gaussians whose entropy has no general closed-form solution. However, tractable approximations exist: variational lower bounds, moment-matching to a single Gaussian (H≈12log⁡det⁡(2πeΣmix)H \approx \frac{1}{2}\log\det(2\pi e\, \Sigma_{\text{mix}}) where Σmix\Sigma_{\text{mix}} is the covariance of the mixture), or Monte Carlo estimation of the log-density via the mixture’s explicit form. A discrete codebook representation (e.g., VQ-VAE) offers an alternative route entirely, reducing entropy estimation to combinatorial counting over code indices: H=−∑ipilog⁡piH = -\sum_i p_i \log p_i. In either case, the compression architecture and the entropy estimator are co-designed: the representational format is chosen (or learned) precisely so that the empowerment-relevant quantities are cheap to compute.

Neural architecture; how is it evolutionarily instantiated as an architectural prior? The concepts are summarized schematically (Figure).

The brain’s practical route to entropies over St+kS_{t+k} is not explicit −!∫plog⁡p-!\int p\log p integration in pixel/joint space, but an architectural prior that (i) compresses sensorimotor state into task-relevant latents and (ii) represents (and can rapidly manipulate) uncertainty/precision within those latents.

Sensory cortical hierarchies perform massive, progressive dimensionality reduction:  10610^6 retinal ganglion axons project through LGN to V1, which then feeds a cascade of extrastriate areas extracting increasingly abstract, lower-dimensional features (edges -> textures -> object parts -> object identity). Analogous hierarchies exist in somatosensory, auditory, and proprioceptive pathways. By the time sensory information reaches associative and prefrontal regions–where action-relevant state evaluation plausibly occurs–the representational space has been compressed by orders of magnitude relative to the raw receptor sheet. This compression is not generic: it is shaped by evolutionary priors (genetically specified cytoarchitectonic boundaries, laminar connectivity motifs, topographic gradients established by molecular cues like ephrins) that constrain the cortical hierarchy to extract the sensorimotor-relevant degrees of freedom–object positions, body-configuration variables, agent-relevant affordances–while discarding task-irrelevant variation. This is precisely the kind of compression that renders downstream entropy estimation tractable. The concepts are summarized schematically (Figure).

Within these compressed representations, neural populations appear to encode not point estimates of state but distributional information–probability distributions over latent state variables–through what have been termed Probabilistic Population Codes (PPCs) (see "Representing Uncertainty"). In such codes, the pattern of firing rates across a population specifies the parameters of an approximate (often near-Gaussian) posterior distribution, while trial-to-trial variability and noise correlations carry information about uncertainty. This format is significant because it makes entropy-related quantities directly "readable" by downstream circuits: the width or covariance of the encoded distribution–which is monotonically related to its entropy–is available in the population activity pattern itself, without requiring an explicit logarithmic computation.

For approximately Gaussian population codes, the conditional entropy H(Zt+k|zt,at:t+k)H(Z_{t+k}|z_t,a_{t:t+k}) is determined (up to a constant) by the log-determinant of the predictive covariance, which can in principle be read out from the gain or dispersion of the population response encoding predicted future states. Forward models in motor-related circuits (across the hierarchy) produce predictions about future states with associated uncertainty, providing exactly the predictive distributions P(zt+k|zt,at:t+k)P(z_{t+k}|z_t,a_{t:t+k}) whose spread determines the conditional entropy term.

For the marginal entropy H(Zt+k|zt)H(Z_{t+k}|z_t)–requiring marginalization over actions–the brain need not compute the entropy of the full mixture analytically. Instead, a population that aggregates predictions across multiple candidate action sequences (e.g., via parallel cortico-basal ganglia loops evaluating different action candidates) would exhibit compound variability reflecting both the per-action predictive uncertainty and the across-action spread of predicted outcomes. The total variance (or second-moment statistics) of such a population implicitly encodes a moment-matched approximation to the mixture entropy. This is the neural analogue of the ∑mix\sum_{mix} approximation described above: downstream circuits can read the marginal entropy as the overall dispersion of predicted-future-state representations, without ever explicitly representing or integrating over the mixture density.

The key architectural point is that evolution did not separately optimize a compression scheme and an entropy estimator; it shaped cortical representations so that the format of the compressed code is simultaneously the substrate for entropy readout. The approximately Gaussian, smoothly topographic character of many cortical population codes is not merely a consequence of efficient coding for perception–it is also an evolved architectural prior that makes predictive-uncertainty quantities (and thereby empowerment) cheap to extract. The convergence of anatomical projections from sensory hierarchies, cerebellar forward-model outputs, and action-candidate representations onto common integrative regions (posterior parietal cortex, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex) instantiates the co-design principle at the level of neural circuitry: the compression, prediction, and entropy-estimation functions are physically wired to interact.
